checks.detail: ping/pong heartbeat found — half-open sockets get reaped. Clients should auto-reconnect with snapshot-then-stream (the §3.5 pattern) since blue-green cutover severs every live socket.

checks.title: Readiness gate pattern detected in /healthz
checks.detail: ready gated on `backfillDone && feed.connected`; contract fields present: ready, live, checks (§N2 pinned shape {live, ready, checks: {...}}).

checks.title: Ingestion reconnects with backoff
checks.detail: A reconnect-with-backoff pattern is present in the ingestion path.

checks.title: Last-tick age surfaced in /healthz
checks.detail: Feed staleness is its own metric with its own Finding class (§N2/§N3): P2 at most, market-calendar-aware, and NEVER a reconciler restart trigger — feed silence is the normal state most of the week.

checks.title: Backfill resumes from checkpoint with bounded concurrency
checks.detail: Resume-from-checkpoint plus bounded request concurrency found — restarts do not re-pull full history (§N4 rate-limit guidance).

checks.title: Exclusive upstream feeds require the recreate strategy
checks.detail: Detected: alpaca. These permit one concurrent websocket per account — during a blue-green overlap two ingestion daemons fight over the socket (green never becomes ready, or kicks blue's live feed mid-serving), and a double backfill can exhaust quotas. deploy_strategy is set to recreate in the manifest (§N4).
checks.fix_hint: Keep the recreate strategy (the manifest already pins it), or add a documented pre-stop ingestion-handoff hook (a `prestop`/handoff script that pauses ingestion) if blue-green is truly needed.

checks.title: Local on-disk state — single-instance site
checks.detail: Data files: data/app.sqlite3, data/app.sqlite3-wal, data/bars-2026-01.parquet, data/levels.duckdb. State on host disk means single-instance only (§9.5.6) — marked, not blocked; correct for v1. deploy_strategy is set to recreate and the data directory becomes a per-Site named volume (§N1/N5). SQLite present: WAL does not make concurrent cross-container writers safe — the old writer must stop before the new one writes. DuckDB files are derived data, rebuildable from Parquet — excluded from backup (§N6).
checks.fix_hint: Keep the data directory on the named volume the manifest declares (never in image layers); backups ride the per-site data-backup registry (sqlite_file + incremental directory_sync, §N6).

checks.title: Broker credentials are env-driven — prefer read-only/paper keys
checks.detail: Broker key env names found in .env.example: ALPACA_KEY_ID, ALPACA_SECRET, FINMIND_TOKEN. Env-driven is correct; committed key-like values ride core.secret-scan (entropy scan §4.5). Keyless Binance endpoints need no secret.
checks.fix_hint: Broker keys are a money-moving credential class (§M4): use read-only or paper-trading keys wherever the broker supports scoping, store live keys in the vault, and never commit .env.

checks.title: Backtesting is manual-only in v1
checks.detail: The Python offline component (duckdb, polars, vectorbt) cannot run inside the Node-only production image. v1 ships backtesting as manual-only (§N7); the manifest records a jobs_image stub from pyproject.toml so the Phase-3 run-image-X-with-volumes job type can pick it up.
checks.fix_hint: Run backtests manually against the same Parquet data for now; when the Phase-3 job type lands, the jobs_image container shares the site's Parquet volume read-only.
